speaker: lucretia
personality: Cold, exact Porto informant who trades only in facts and money; despises speeches, flattery and wasted time.

openings.text: Half the street watched you walk over here, and the Federation has the district on edge. You have one minute.
You're the one asking questions around the Porto. Asking questions is how people end up on a truck. What do you want?

exchanges.prompt: I don't do causes. I do information, and information costs. Who sent you?

replies.text: People who want Napoli free. People like you, if you'd let yourself admit it.
replies.reaction: Don't tell me what I am. You don't know me.

replies.text: Friends of friends. Ask around. You'll hear I pay.
replies.reaction: I have asked. Apparently you do.

replies.text: Nobody you want to know. I'm here to buy, and I don't waste a seller's time.
replies.reaction: Good answer. Short ones usually are.

replies.text: Here's {cost}. Call it a deposit, not an answer.
replies.reaction: A deposit. All right, you've bought yourself one conversation.

exchanges.prompt: Everyone in this city sells something. Legionaries sell passes, the prefecture sells names. Why should I sell to you and not to them?

replies.text: Because I won't come back with soldiers, and I don't haggle over good information.
replies.reaction: Two things the prefecture can't promise. Noted.

replies.text: Because if you sell to them, people like me will remember it.
replies.reaction: Threats. From someone standing alone in my street.

replies.text: I don't know. Maybe you shouldn't.
replies.reaction: At least you're not pretending.

exchanges.prompt: Last thing. Do you know how many trucks leave the Castel in a week? I do. I count them. Why would someone like you care?

replies.text: Because what's in those trucks is why I'm in Napoli.
replies.reaction: Is it. Everyone cares about the trucks until it costs them something.

replies.text: You don't need to believe I care. Tell me the count, and watch what I do with it.
replies.reaction: Fourteen, last week. We'll see what you do with it.

replies.text: You count them because you care. I can tell.
replies.reaction: I count them because counts sell. Don't make it a story.

closings.success: Fine. You've earned an answer without paying for it. Don't get used to that.
closings.failure: We're done. Walk away, and don't be surprised who I describe you to.
closings.rebuff: Not yet. I don't sell to strangers. Come back, and we'll see if you're still one.
closings.bribed: Money is the one thing in this city that doesn't lie. Listen carefully. I won't repeat it.

speaker: lucretia
personality: The informant on a second meeting: transactional, testing whether the agent is worth the risk; rewards fair trades and precision, punishes sentiment and pressure.

openings.text: The one who pays. Money buys answers, not friends. What are you buying tonight?
You came back. Most people I turn away don't. That's either brave or stupid.
Still breathing. Good. I wondered if you'd make it back.
You again. Sit. Keep your back to the window.

exchanges.prompt: I didn't sell your description to anyone. That cost me money. So what are you bringing me in return?

replies.text: A small one. The Porto gate legionary takes Federation vouchers to look away.
replies.reaction: Small, but true, and free. It's a start.

replies.text: My gratitude. That should count for something.
replies.reaction: Gratitude doesn't pay rent.

replies.text: Federation patrol changes in the Porto. Times and routes. Yours, no charge.
replies.reaction: That's worth something. You've done this before.

replies.text: {cost}, and you tell me what I need without the bargaining.
replies.reaction: Simple. I like simple.

exchanges.prompt: The trucks take people to the Castel, and nobody comes out. I keep a list of who goes in. I'm looking for one name. Seen anything I can't buy?

replies.text: I have their transport manifest. Fourteen names out of the Castel, routed to Pier 9.
replies.reaction: He's not on it. So he's already gone, or he's still in there.

replies.text: Not yet. Give me the name, and I'll look for it where you can't go.
replies.reaction: Not yet, maybe next time. But that's the right offer.

replies.text: One name? Everyone's lost someone. Why does yours matter more?
replies.reaction: You'd better hope you never find out.

replies.text: No. Nothing.
replies.reaction: Then I'm not sure why we're talking.

exchanges.prompt: You're useful. That makes you dangerous to know. Give me one reason not to sell you to Hale's people when you walk out.

replies.text: Because I'm worth more to you coming back than sold once.
replies.reaction: Repeat business. You understand me better than you did.

replies.text: Because it would be wrong. You're not like them.
replies.reaction: You've no idea what I'm like.

replies.text: Because Hale's people pay late and lie about the price.
replies.reaction: They do. That's true.

closings.success: Fine. You've earned it. Here's what I have.
closings.failure: No. I've given you enough of my time. Walk, and hope nobody asks me about you.
closings.rebuff: Better. Not enough. Come back and keep surprising me.
closings.bribed: Paid in full. That's the only kind of trust I deal in tonight. Listen.

speaker: lucretia
personality: The informant with a missing brother; respects competence and honesty without pity, and is starting to want an ally more than a buyer.

openings.text: You paid last time. You could keep paying. Or you could give me a reason to help you for nothing.
After last time, I nearly sent someone else to meet you. Talk.
You keep coming back. I've stopped selling your description to anyone. I wanted you to know that.
Sit down. I held something back for you. That's not something I do.
You came back. People usually don't, after the second time. Sit.
You again. I'm starting to expect you. I don't like expecting people.

exchanges.prompt: The name I'm looking for is Tito Esposito. My brother. They took him at the fish market in the spring. Every time we meet, I'll ask. Anything?

replies.text: He's probably dead. Most of them are.
replies.reaction: Careful. I know what probably means.

replies.text: Nothing yet. I won't pretend otherwise.
replies.reaction: Good. I've had enough people pretend.

replies.text: His name might be on this. A transport manifest from the Castel, with names and blood types.
replies.reaction: Why would they need blood types? Give it to me, I need to read every line.

replies.text: Nothing yet. But his name is with my people now. If he surfaces, you'll know first.
replies.reaction: First. All right, that's worth more than you know.

exchanges.prompt: For a year after he went, I sold information to the Federation. I thought it would buy him back. Does that disgust you?

replies.text: No. You did what you thought would bring him home. Now you're doing it with me.
replies.reaction: You don't flatter and you don't preach. I can work with that.

replies.text: It does. People died for what you sold.
replies.reaction: Yes, I know. I count those too.

replies.text: It's not my place to judge. I'm here for what you know now.
replies.reaction: Practical. Fine.

replies.text: I'm not here to judge. Here's {cost}. Let's keep it simple between us.
replies.reaction: You'd think I'd prefer simple. Fine.

exchanges.prompt: If I help you properly, not for money, it's my neck as much as yours. Tell me this goes somewhere.

replies.text: It goes to people who've been fighting the Federation much longer than I have.
replies.reaction: Longer isn't better. But fine.

replies.text: I can't promise anything.
replies.reaction: No. Nobody can.

replies.text: It goes to the Castel. To Hale. To whoever put your brother on that truck.
replies.reaction: Then we want the same man. Good.

closings.success: All right. Not for money this time. Here's what I have.
closings.failure: No. I thought you were different. Go, before I decide you're not.
closings.rebuff: Almost. I'm close to trusting you, and that frightens me more than Hale does. Come back.
closings.bribed: Money again. Fine, it works. But I'd hoped we were past that.
